name: CRON_TWIN_GUARD_LQ991_20261108
comment: ANCHOR: CRON_TWIN_GUARD_LQ991_20261108 — LQ-20261107-991: a lane live on n8n must not still own a firing cron line.
Fable's n8n design audit (LQ-984 Q6 #1/#14) measured 37 lines by matching a lane's script basename. Measured
2026-11-08T16:41Z against the 723-row registry: 25 lanes own 26 firing lines; eleven of the 37 were a sibling
lane's line running the same script with different arguments, which the audit mis-attributed.
The gate compares registry dispatch.mode=live to a sanitized committed snapshot of the crontab
(config/crontab_snapshot.txt, captured_at stamped, /home/<user> replaced by $HOME). A stale or unstamped
snapshot is CANNOT RUN (exit 2), never clean. Attribution is by tag, effect-claim wrapper, scheduler.match,
then script+arguments; a tie is reported ambiguous and assigned to nobody, so the gate never proposes to
comment a line it cannot name.
The inherited-debt baseline (config/cron_twin_baseline.json) holds today's 26 findings and can only shrink:
after the operator runs comment-cron, regenerate the snapshot and re-emit the baseline with --prune-baseline.
Tests are hermetic: synthetic registry rows and crontab text; one test grades the committed snapshot and
baseline so the gate is proven green on the day it lands. No crontab command, no systemd, no database.
